Assessment updated with SLOOS: The FOMC statement is restrictive (another 75 bp hike to 2.25–2.50%, continued QT) amid elevated inflation and war-related headwinds, with labor markets still strong. The July 2022 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates a further tightening in the credit channel: banks tightened standards and terms for C&I loans across firm sizes and for CRE; increased loan pricing and collateralization; and tightened for several consumer categories (credit cards, subprime auto, jumbo and GSE-eligible mortgages, HELOCs). Banks cited a weaker economic outlook and liquidity concerns, and reported weaker demand for CRE loans, though demand was firmer for some categories (HELOCs, C&I for small firms). This broad-based tightening in bank lending conditions amplifies the restrictive stance and downside growth risks, outweighing pockets of resilience. Net tone: more negative than the FSR-adjusted baseline.
